name: Qurayt ibn Unayf
bio: Qurayt ibn Unayf belonged to Banu al-Anbar, a branch of Tamim. Al-Zirikli places him before Islam, while the introduction to his verses in al-Tibrizi’s Hamasa commentary calls him an Islamic poet. Almost all that survives about his life turns on the loss of his camels to Shayban and the help he sought from Mazin, in a story al-Zirikli traces to Abu Ubayda. Abu Tammam opened his Hamasa with the verses under the name of the tribe, and al-Tibrizi preserves Abu al-Nada’s attribution to Qurayt. His date of death is unknown.
